essenceNote: Kenya's foreign languages at Junior School are Arabic, French, German, and Mandarin — each a non-formal, basic (A1/YCT2-equivalent) 4-skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing) curriculum, taught in an experiential, innovative and flexible program guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories (verbatim essence statement, identical wording to the Grade 9 French design).

notes: Grade 8 French preserves the same 3-strand / 9-theme structure seen at Grade 9 (Greetings, Family, My Surrounding, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Foods and Drinks, My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around — same 9 themes, same order) = 27 distinct sub-strands (9 themes x 3 strands), confirmed verbatim against the PDF's own SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUBSTRANDS table and per-theme tables. Unlike the Grade 9 designs, Grade 8's summary table lists sub-strand *types* generically (e.g. 'Interactive speaking', 'Reading for understanding', 'Guided writing') rather than the per-theme sub-strand names seen inline in each theme's table — the per-theme names/codes (1.1-1.9, 2.1-2.9, 3.1-3.9) used here are read directly from each theme's own strand table, which is the more specific/authoritative source. Content differs meaningfully from Grade 9: Grade 8 leans more grammar/register-focused (formal 'vous' politeness register, imperative mood for travel instructions, word-order/orthography drills) versus Grade 9's more vocabulary-recall-focused approach, even though the theme labels are the same. Total suggested lessons: 27 (Listening & Speaking) + 18 (Reading) + 9 (Writing) = 54, plus 6 lessons for showcasing, matching German Grade 8's allocation exactly.
